messages:
Alex: FYI support escalated two enterprise customers experiencing p95/p99 spikes and intermittent 500/504s on their Dedicated pools around 11:18 UTC. They report timeouts and tail latency from our hosted endpoint.

Maria: Looking at dashboards now. p95 for dedicated-prod-gpu-b climbed from ~140ms -> ~1.6s; p99 spiked to ~3.2s. Spike duration ~6 minutes 11:18-11:24. The attach latency histogram also shows a concentrated bump.

Jordan: Customer repro they provided is: steady 30 rps, then a sudden variant switch + 80 rps burst. Autoscaler requested new instances; many requests were routed to nodes in the attach state. Logs show repeated "AttachLatency" events >2s and several requests that later timed out on client side.

Olivia: PromQL snippets I ran:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{pool="dedicated-prod-gpu-b"}[2m])) by (le))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(attach_latency_seconds_bucket{pool="dedicated-prod-gpu-b"}[5m])) by (le))
```
Both confirm tail hurt.

Sam: Autoscaler traces show a provider provisioning backlog: instance create -> provisioning -> gpu driver install -> gpu ready. Provider returned intermittent 429s for create during the wave; retry backoff extended provisioning from ~40s -> ~120s.

support-bot: Escalation created #4589 (severity=high) for Acme Retail. Attach traces attached.

Alex: Immediate mitigation ideas:
- Prefer routing to prewarmed variants for these customers during the incident
- Temporarily raise min_reserved_instances for their pools
- Change attach policy so attaching nodes refuse traffic (fast 429) instead of accepting and stalling requests
I'll try route preference and set attaching->reject for 10m.

deploy-bot: route override `prefer-prewarm-dedicated-acme` applied -> OK
deploy-bot: pool flag `reject_attaching_requests=true` for dedicated-prod-gpu-b -> OK

Jordan: After route override p95 dropped to ~180ms in ~45s. p99 came down to ~650ms but some outliers persist from mmapping. We're still seeing a few 500s from nodes that reported "mmapping model" and then returned 5xx.

Maria: Cloud provider acknowledged a brief quota throttling event in us-west-2 11:12-11:26 UTC. Ticket open with provider (CP-998877). They reported elevated create latencies when AZ throttled requests.

Sam: Short-term ops items:
1) Increase min_reserved_instances from 1 -> 5 for Acme's dedicated pool for 24h to avoid immediate scale-ups.
2) Keep `reject_attaching_requests=true` for 15m then revert.
3) Deploy a warmup-run job that does model mmap + 3 short inference calls after GPU ready.
4) Add a small immediate retry on attach path to route to an available warm node before queuing.

Olivia: Warmup job sketch (idempotent):
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
for i in $(seq 1 5); do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $WARMUP_KEY" https://internal-infer.local/v1/models/$MODEL:predict -d '{"inputs":["warmup"]}' || true
  sleep 1
done
```
I'll template this and roll as an opt-in for pools.

Jordan: Dev idea: on attach, check `node.ready && mmap_complete`. If not, return a fast 429 with header `x-attach-state: not-ready` so routing can fallback. Pseudocode:
```
if (!node.ready || !node.mmap_done) return HTTP_429("attach-not-ready");
```
We should also instrument timings: attach_start, instance_create_time, gpu_ready_time, mmap_complete_time, first_successful_infer_time.

Sam: I'll add those telemetry fields to attach traces and store them in our traces index. That'll help quantify where the long pole is.

Maria: I'll draft a short incident summary for customers and a detailed postmortem. Timeline + metrics + actions. Target: 48h for full postmortem, 6h for short config fix.

Alex: Customer comms: told Acme were routing away from attaching nodes, increased reserved capacity temporarily, and opened provider ticket. They want a root cause and plan to avoid recurrence.

deploy-bot: scheduled revert of `reject_attaching_requests` flag in 15m (2161235467). Will annotate if manual cancel requested.

Olivia: Runbook note added to #runbooks: steps for toggling route overrides, bumping reserved instances, running warmup jobs, and contacting provider.

Jordan: Commands useful for debugging:
```
kubectl logs -l app=pool-manager -c pool-manager --since=3h | rg "PROVISIONING|AttachLatency|mmapping" -i
rg "mmapping model" /var/log/worker/*.log | tail -n 200
```
Also Grep traces index for attach durations > 1s.

Sam: Follow-ups: PR to add opt-in warmup-runner to the autoscaler, config switch per-customer for `min_reserved_instances`, and a safe-attach gating change.

Alex: Thanks all. Keeping this channel live until provider ticket resolved and we revert flags. Ping @oncall if p99 > 1s reoccurs. :thumbsup:
